output.summary: An evergreen tree endemic to New Zealand, karaka is mainly coastal, though it also grows inland in the North Island. It has thick, leathery green leaves and oval yellow-orange fruit. Māori ate the uncooked fruit flesh and the highly poisonous seeds only after lengthy detoxification.
output.edibilityNote: Māori ate the fruit flesh uncooked; the highly poisonous seeds required lengthy detoxification before consumption.
